reader.requirement: A procedure-name of a declarative (USE) section may be referenced from a different declarative section or from the nondeclarative portion only by PERFORM (alone or THRU). A GO TO (simple or DEPENDING), an ALTER (either operand) or a SORT/MERGE INPUT/OUTPUT PROCEDURE that names it from outside its own section is refused; references inside the same section are free. A USE FOR DEBUGGING section's procedures may not be referenced from outside the debugging sections at all (XV.3.2.3 SR3).
reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|IsActive|Constructs|CobolVersion|Edition.Edition in StatementValidation.CheckDeclarativesBoundary and ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedureOperand: none. data.Edition.Error is the diagnostic sink, not an edition test. The debugging-section arm runs only when WITH DEBUGGING MODE compiled a debugging section, which is a property of the source, not a --std test.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same funnel and severity at every edition (the doc comment says 'Every edition')

reader.notes: Every statement that takes a procedure-name resolves through ResolveProcedureOperand, which asks CheckDeclarativesBoundary by section identity. Only PERFORM (and RESUME, which 1985 lacks) is exempt. Each verb that can reference a procedure was probed in both directions.

refuter.evidence: Probes beyond the reader's (refute-1985-025/src/use3ok2.cob, u3x_*.cob, --std 85). Legal half, no over-rejection: PERFORM P1 OF D1 THRU P4 OF D1 from main, GO TO P3 OF D1 (qualified) and GO TO P4 DEPENDING ON K inside D1, PERFORM P1 OF D2 2 TIMES, PERFORM D2 VARYING ... UNTIL, GO TO P1 OF MAINSEC and an unqualified GO TO P1 from MAINSEC while P1 also names a paragraph of D1 and D2 -> all compile and run (N=0003/0023/0043/1043; LOCAL-P1). (use3ok2-002 was my own program falling out of a PERFORM range into a recursive PERFORM: a program error, stack overflow, not evidence; -003 is the corrected program.) Refusal half: MERGE ... OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS D1, SORT ... OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS P1 OF D1, SORT ... INPUT PROCEDURE IS M9 THRU D1 (declarative as the THRU end) -> each COBOL2376. Side note, not a GR3 defect: at --std 85 COBOL2376 quotes and cites §2023:14.9.49.3 SR4 instead of §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR3, while COBOL6946 cites §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR3. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR3.
